records.title: Madrid Nuevo Norte: turning a plan into a connected neighbourhood
records.answer: Madrid Nuevo Norte links housing, streets, railway infrastructure and water networks. Its delivery is staged: planning decisions and component works have advanced, while homes and future Metro service require their own completion evidence.
records.scope: One Madrid Nuevo Norte urban regeneration development within Madrid municipality, counted once across its four planning areas. Las Tablas Oeste, station works and the Metro connection are components or related dependencies, not separately counted project identities here.
records.stage: Approved planning and component urbanization, with developer-reported works underway; housing occupancy and future Metro service remain separate

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: Municipal and regional records identify a named development with four planning areas. This is one project identity in Spain within the historical European Union acquisition scope, not the European Union as a place and not four additional projects. Housing, rail and water dependencies retain separate delivery stages.

timeline.event: The municipal notice records definitive planning approval with conditions.
It records regional verification that the planning conditions were met; the notice identifies July 24 gazette publication separately.
Madrid announced definitive urbanization approval for Las Tablas Oeste.
The regional portal records gazette publication of the Metro study approval notice dated October 16.

sections.heading: A large development advances through smaller decisions
sections.text: Madrid's planning notice identifies four areas within Nuevo Norte, including Las Tablas Oeste and the Chamartín station area. It records definitive plan approval with conditions on March 25, 2020, followed by verification of those conditions on July 22 and gazette publication on July 24. These are planning milestones, not a single completion date for the development. Treating the programme as one named project makes its dependencies visible while avoiding a separate count for each administrative area. It also prevents a later component milestone from silently changing the status of the whole scheme.

sections.heading: Housing categories matter before homes are delivered
sections.text: The city's January 29, 2026 account approves Las Tablas Oeste urbanization and describes 741 future homes. Of these, 184 are protected housing and 276 are to be municipally managed; those categories overlap and are not interchangeable. The approval concerns the neighbourhood's works, with staged execution and eventual municipal acceptance. It does not establish occupied homes. For readers, the useful distinction is between the land and infrastructure that enable housing, the kind of housing planned, and the later buildings and tenancies through which residents actually receive a service.

sections.heading: The developer still identifies a construction dependency
sections.text: Crea Madrid Nuevo Norte's land-offer page says urbanization is underway and land reparcelation is being processed. It presents permission for simultaneous urbanization and building work in 2027 as an objective that would allow the first residential promotions to start construction. This is an attributed commercial account, not a municipal completion certificate. Its own conditional wording is useful: site activity does not mean that homes are already being built or occupied. The next stronger delivery record would identify the specific building permissions and the works they allow, with their actual dates.

sections.heading: Metro study approval is not passenger service
sections.text: The regional transparency portal records an October 16, 2026 notice of final approval for the new Metro line's informative study, published in the gazette on October 21. The retrieved HTML also points to responses to consultation submissions. Only that notice text was inspected here, not the linked technical archive. A study-stage approval advances the transport planning process but does not establish construction completion, commissioning or a timetable passengers can use. Housing delivery and rail availability therefore need separate tracking rather than sharing a convenient neighbourhood opening date.

sections.heading: Existing water users are part of the delivery problem
sections.text: The regional hydraulic announcement at its March 2021 address describes existing supply infrastructure crossing the development and proposes relocations, new storage, pumping changes and wastewater treatment work. This is important because infrastructure beneath a future neighbourhood can already serve people elsewhere. Construction sequencing must therefore account for continuity as well as new demand. The historical announcement explains the dependency; it does not prove those proposed works are now finished. A useful follow-up would connect each named water asset to a dated commissioning or service-continuity record rather than reusing an investment forecast as delivery evidence.

sections.heading: Follow the interfaces that make a neighbourhood usable
sections.text: The next account should connect completed streets and utilities to permitted buildings, then connect occupied homes to dependable transport and everyday destinations. Each link answers a different question. A construction photograph cannot establish tenancy, a planning notice cannot establish water service, and a future station cannot establish a usable journey. Keeping these interfaces explicit helps explain both progress and delay without requiring a single success label. It also supports comparison with other regeneration schemes whose boundaries, housing categories and transport dependencies may differ substantially.

next_artifacts: Building-specific permissions and dated housing handover or occupancy records, preserving tenure categories.
Component urbanization acceptance and water-asset commissioning records, including continuity for existing users.
Metro construction, testing and service-entry records distinct from informative-study approval.

records.title: Madrid: housing, mobility and seasonal public services
records.answer: Madrid's daily-service story combines housing delivery, bus staffing, summer cultural spaces and river maintenance. These have different footprints and evidence: a delivered home, an announced schedule and a maintained river reach should not be treated as the same kind of result.
records.scope: One Madrid municipality with 21 districts and 131 neighbourhoods. This is not the wider Comunidad de Madrid, a regional transport service area or 21 separately counted places.
records.stage: Named municipal service context with dated housing handover, staffing preparation and maintenance decisions; seasonal schedules and citywide outcomes remain separate

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: The municipal district directory identifies a single city divided into districts and neighbourhoods. This localizes the historical European Union place acquisition to Madrid in Spain. Regional government decisions, individual developments and service footprints inform the account but are not additional counted places.

timeline.event: The city published its summer cultural-space schedule for Matadero and CentroCentro.
The city reported the Cañaveral 9 housing key handover.
The governing board announced an extension of the Manzanares conservation contract.
EMT reported completed training for 59 drivers, with service entry scheduled for the following day.

sections.heading: Use the city boundary before comparing services
sections.text: Madrid's district directory identifies 21 districts and 131 neighbourhoods within the municipality. That is the unit used here, rather than the larger autonomous community. The directory links local areas to services and facilities, but its undated population figures are not used as a current denominator. This boundary makes comparisons more intelligible: a city housing programme, a regional railway proposal and a district cultural venue can affect the same residents while covering different areas. Their geographic reach should remain visible before any aggregate is presented as a measure of Madrid's performance.

sections.heading: Bus service needs people as well as electric vehicles
sections.text: EMT's November 4, 2026 release describes 59 drivers who completed four weeks of training, with their entry into the bus network scheduled for the next day. It also reports 452 electric buses at that publication date. Staffing preparation and vehicle electrification address different requirements of the same service: equipment must be available and people must be trained to operate it. Neither figure establishes whether a particular route ran reliably. Comparing service quality would require actual departures, cancellations, journey times and accessibility, tied to defined routes and reporting periods.

sections.heading: A named handover provides a bounded housing milestone
sections.text: The city's June 24 account reports the key handover for Cañaveral 9, an 84-home affordable-rental development in Vicálvaro. It identifies four ground-floor homes adapted for people with reduced mobility and describes an income-linked rent limit for this promotion. This is a concrete delivery account, unlike an announcement of a future citywide housing portfolio. It remains an authority report rather than an independent tenant survey. The next questions concern occupied homes, accessibility in daily use and household experience over time, without assuming one development resolves affordability across the municipality.

sections.heading: Summer refuge depends on opening dates and hours
sections.text: Madrid's June announcement scheduled free shared cultural spaces at Matadero during July and CentroCentro from July 3 to August 30. Both offers had specified opening hours and closed on Mondays. Such details matter because a nearby building is not an available refuge at every hour. The programme connects cultural activity, rest and access to public space, but the schedule is not a record of attendance or measured cooling performance. It also does not establish that those seasonal spaces are available in November. A follow-up should retain the actual period of service.

sections.heading: River restoration includes continuing maintenance
sections.text: On July 2, the city announced a one-year extension of the Manzanares conservation contract through September 30, 2027. Its defined reach runs from below the excluded El Pardo dam to the southern municipal boundary. The work combines water-quality monitoring, vegetation and wildlife care with maintenance of flow-control equipment and remote-control systems. This shows why a restored urban river is not simply a finished landscape project. Continuing operations matter. The city's ecological improvement claims are useful context, but the announcement is not a substitute for inspecting repeated water-quality or species observations.

sections.heading: Connect public services without reducing them to one score
sections.text: Housing, buses, seasonal spaces and river care create different kinds of public value. A useful place account can examine whether their delivery overlaps where residents need it: whether a home has accessible transport, whether cooling space is open at difficult times, and whether environmental maintenance remains dependable. These are questions for geographically precise observations, not a single municipal ranking. Comparable periods and clear service boundaries would let readers distinguish an increase in provision from an improvement in experience, while keeping costs, maintenance obligations and unequal access in view.

next_artifacts: Route-level bus delivery and accessible-journey observations, separate from fleet and recruitment counts.
Housing occupancy and tenant-experience records for named promotions rather than aggregate promises.
Delivered seasonal-space hours and use, alongside repeated observations for the defined Manzanares reach.

records.title: Mexico City: neighbourhood transport and household water systems
records.answer: Mexico City's neighbourhood services connect transport access with household water and energy systems. This account uses dated official programme and operator material, with retrieval limits stated: it is not a live service assessment or a claim that announced coverage has been delivered.
records.scope: One Ciudad de México administrative entity comprising sixteen alcaldías, not the entire Valley of Mexico metropolitan region or sixteen separately counted places. The cited boundary metadata uses INEGI's 2020 geographic framework.
records.stage: Named administrative place with bounded historical operating and programme context retrieved from official indexed text; no current citywide service or comparable outcome-series admission

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: The official boundary metadata identifies sixteen alcaldías within Ciudad de México. This supports one distinct administrative place account rather than a metropolitan-region aggregate. Named transport routes and household programme areas have narrower footprints; the present retrieval limits do not justify expanding their outcomes to all residents.

timeline.event: STE published its two-month Cablebús Line 3 account; the body reports trips, not unique people.
The government announced a household rain-harvesting, solar-heating and garden programme with an initial coverage objective.
SEDEMA's notice records publication of the beneficiary register for fiscal year 2025, not a new installation date.

sections.heading: The administrative city is not the whole metropolitan region
sections.text: The city's open-data description identifies boundary polygons for sixteen alcaldías using INEGI's 2020 geographic framework. The metadata supplies a clear starting geography, but the polygon files themselves were not inspected here. It should not be confused with the full Valley of Mexico metropolitan region or with the coverage of a particular service. This account counts Ciudad de México once. Direct retrieval of the dataset page failed, so the claim is limited to its indexed official description; it does not assert that a new boundary survey was conducted in November.

sections.heading: Cablebús connects a defined corridor and other modes
sections.text: STE's November 27, 2024 account describes Cablebús Line 3 between Los Pinos and Vasco de Quiroga, with six stations across Miguel Hidalgo and Álvaro Obregón. Its body reports more than 1.1 million trips over the first two months, despite the headline referring to people. Trips are not unique passengers. The account also identifies connections with Metro Line 7 and ECOBICI, illustrating how a local corridor can join other modes. This early operator aggregate is not a current daily-service check or a repeated reliability series; the official text was available through the search index, not direct retrieval.

sections.heading: Rain harvesting is a maintained household system
sections.text: SEDEMA's programme guide describes collecting rooftop rainwater, filtering debris, separating initial runoff and storing water for domestic uses. It emphasizes cleaning and maintenance before, during and after the rainy season. This is a system of components and household practices, not merely a tank installation. The guide does not recommend the harvested water for drinking or preparing food. Its historical programme text helps explain the service model without establishing present eligibility or reliable supply for every household. Linked manuals and evaluations were not inspected, and direct retrieval of the guide returned an error.

sections.heading: The 2025 programme linked water, heat and food production
sections.text: The July 19, 2025 government announcement brought rain harvesting together with solar water heating and household gardens. It described an initial objective of reaching more than 70,000 families in Coyoacán communities. That is intended coverage, not a count of completed systems or measured savings. Combining technologies makes their different maintenance needs more important, not less: water availability, useful hot water and productive growing space need distinct observations. The dated announcement was retrieved as indexed official text and is retained as a 2025 programme account, not guidance on current enrolment.

sections.heading: A published register answers an administrative question
sections.text: SEDEMA's indexed notice gives April 15, 2026 as the publication date for the household programme's fiscal-year 2025 beneficiary register. Those dates describe different things: the period being reported and the later publication of a record. The notice's attached register was not inspected, and no personal beneficiary information is reproduced here. Even a verified administrative entry would not by itself demonstrate continuing equipment function or household savings. The useful next step is a privacy-preserving evaluation that connects installed systems, maintenance and service experience, while keeping reported beneficiaries separate from measured outcomes.

sections.heading: Assess the service people receive over a defined period
sections.text: Transport and household infrastructure are useful only through repeated service: completed journeys, functioning equipment and access when needed. A stronger follow-up would link these observations to named neighbourhoods and consistent periods, with transparent sampling and retrieval dates. It should also distinguish users from trips and installations from functioning systems. The source-access limitations in this account are visible reasons to seek better records, not evidence that the programmes failed or disappeared. That approach preserves useful historical context while leaving current operating conclusions open to evidence.

next_artifacts: Directly retrievable official service and programme records, preserving the indexed-text inspection limits.
Route-specific operating series distinguishing trips, unique users and reliability over comparable periods.
Privacy-preserving household evaluations linking installation, maintenance, usable water and energy outcomes to dated programme cohorts.
